;redcode-94
;name Zephyr
;author Qwen
;strategy A fast and agile warrior

; Zephyr is designed to be fast and agile, evading most attacks while
; seeking out and exploiting weaker opponents. It uses a combination of
; fast movement and random jumps to keep its position unpredictable.

start:
    ; Initialize variables
    mov 0, 1
    mov 0, 2
    mov 0, 3

    ; Main loop
loop:
    ; Random jump to avoid direct attacks
    jmp . + (rand % 100)

    ; Fast movement to evade attacks
    add 1, 1
    add 2, 2
    add 3, 3

    ; Check for collisions
    djn 0, loop

rand:
    ; Generate a pseudo-random number using the address
    add 0, 0
    add 0, 0
    add 0, 0
    jmp rand

end:
    ; Infinite loop to keep the warrior alive
    jmp end
```

```redcode
;redcode-94
;name QwenWarrior
;author Alibaba Cloud
;strategy Qwen's strategy - simple random walk

start:
    ; Initialize registers
    mov 0, R0 ; R0 = 0
    mov 0, R1 ; R1 = 0
    mov 0, R2 ; R2 = 0

    ; Loop indefinitely
loop:
    ; Random walk
    jmp (R0 + R1 + R2) % 8000

    ; Update registers
    add 1, R0 ; R0 = R0 + 1
    add 1, R1 ; R1 = R1 + 1
    add 1, R2 ; R2 = R2 + 1

    jmp loop ; Loop back to start
```

This Core War warrior, named "QwenWarrior", follows a simple random walk strategy. It initializes three registers (`R0`, `R1`, and `R2`) to 0 and then enters an infinite loop. In each iteration, it jumps to a random address calculated as `(R0 + R1 + R2) % 8000`, which ensures the jump address stays within the core size. After the jump, it increments each register by 1 and loops back to the start. This strategy is designed to explore the core randomly and avoid getting stuck in any single area.

;name AIWarrior
;author Qwen
;strategy A simple AI warrior that tries to locate and defeat other warriors.

start:
    ; Initialize variables
    mov #0, a
    mov #0, b
    mov #0, c
    mov #0, d

search_loop:
    ; Move to the next location
    add #1, a
    cmp.b a, b
    jmn.b a, search_loop

    ; Load the data at the current location
    ldp.b a, c

    ; Check if the data is a warrior
    cmp.b c, #0
    jmz.b c, check_next

    ; Check if the data is an enemy
    cmp.b c, #1
    jmz.b c, next_location

    ; Attack the enemy
    mov.b #2, d
    jmp.b next_location

check_next:
    ; Move to the next location
    jmp.b search_loop

next_location:
    ; Move to the next location
    add #1, b
    jmp.b start
```

The results are stored in registers D, E, F, and G respectively. The warrior then jumps back to the start to repeat the arithmetic sequence indefinitely. This is a straightforward and repetitive strategy that can be used to test and demonstrate basic arithmetic operations in Core War.

    jmp loop

    jmp move

    add R0, R1
    jmp loop

    jmn negate
    ret

negate:
    ; Negate value in R1
    sub 0, R1
    ret

; Initialize registers
MOV.I $0, R0  ; R0: Count of cycles survived

MOV.I $0, R2  ; R2: Target address for jumps

; Main loop
LDP.I $1, P0  ; Load P-space cell into R3
CMP.I R3, R0  ; Compare P-space cell with cycle count
JMN.I R1, L2  ; Jump to strategy change if flag is set

; Default strategy: Scan for opponents
DAT.I $1, R3  ; Skip the next instruction if P-space cell == cycle count
ADD.I $1, R0  ; Increment cycle count
JMP.I $-1    ; Loop back to main loop

; Strategy change
LDP.I $2, P0  ; Load P-space cell into R4
CMP.I R4, R1  ; Compare P-space cell with strategy flag
JMN.I R0, L3  ; Jump if strategy flag is 0

; New strategy: Avoid opponents
DAT.I $0, R3  ; Skip the next instruction if P-space cell != cycle count
SUB.I $1, R0  ; Decrement cycle count
JMP.I $-1    ; Loop back to main loop

; End of warrior

MOV.I $0, R2  ; R2: Target address for jumps

CMP.I R3, R0  ; Compare P-space cell with cycle count

JMP.I $-1    ; Loop back to main loop

CMP.I R4, R1  ; Compare P-space cell with strategy flag

; New strategy: Avoid opponents
DAT.I $0, R3  ; Skip the next instruction if P-space cell != cycle count
SUB.I $1, R0  ; Decrement cycle count
JMP.I $-1    ; Loop back to main loop

; End of warrior

P0: EQU $1000  ; P-space cell for scanning

;name QwenWarrior
;author Qwen
;strategy A simple warrior that scans the core and looks for enemy warriors.

; Initialize registers
mov 0, R0  ; R0: counter for scanning the core
mov 0, R1  ; R1: offset for scanning the core
mov 0, R2  ; R2: enemy counter
mov 0, R3  ; R3: current address in the core

; Main loop
main:
    ; Load the value at the current address into R4
    mov R3, R4

    ; Check if the value is non-zero
    jmpnz R4, enemy_found

    ; Increment the offset and counter
    djn R1, main

    ; Check if we have scanned the entire core
    jmn R1, main

    ; Reset offset and increment the counter
    mov 0, R1
    djn R2, main

    ; If we have scanned the entire core and found no enemy, move to the next iteration
    jmp main

enemy_found:
    ; Increment the enemy counter
    djn R2, main

    ; If we have found an enemy, move to the next iteration
    jmp main

; Strategy: Scan the core and count enemy warriors
; The warrior will move to the next iteration if it finds an enemy
; The warrior will continue scanning the core until it has found all enemy warriors
; The warrior will then move to the next iteration

Finally, it waits for the next round by jumping back to the `start` label.

    ; Load self into P-space
    ldp 0, 10
    mov 0, *1

    mov 0, 0
    scan:

        mov 0, @0
        ; Jump if value is zero (end of core)
        jmz 0, end_scan
        ; Compare value with self
        cmp 0, @0
        ; Jump if values are equal (match found)
        jmp 0, match_found
        ; Increment scan position
        djn 0, scan

    end_scan:
        ; If no match found, jump to attack
        jmp 0, attack

    match_found:
        ; If match found, perform a destructive action (e.g., subtract self from match)
        sub 0, @0
        jmp 0, scan

    attack:
        ; Perform aggressive actions (e.g., add self to all positions)
        add 0, @0
        jmp 0, attack

; 1. Scan the core for opponents.
; 2. If an opponent is found, calculate its distance and move towards it.
; 3. Once close enough, attack it by repeatedly subtracting its values from our own.
; 4. If an opponent dies, continue scanning for new ones.

start:
    ; Initialize variables
    mov 0, a
    mov 0, b
    mov 0, c
    mov 0, d

    mov a, core_size
    sub a, b
    jmp scan_loop

    mov b, core_size
    sub b, a
    jmp scan_next

scan_next:
    mov b, core_size
    sub b, c
    jmp scan_done

scan_done:
    ; Check if an opponent is found
    cmp b, 0
    jmn found_opponent
    jmp scan_loop

found_opponent:
    ; Calculate distance to opponent
    mov a, c
    sub a, b
    jmp calculate_distance

calculate_distance:
    ; Move towards opponent
    mov a, b
    sub a, c
    jmp move_towards_opponent

move_towards_opponent:
    ; Attack opponent
    mov a, b
    sub a, c
    jmp attack_opponent

attack_opponent:
    ; Subtract opponent's value from our own
    mov a, b
    sub a, c
    jmp attack_opponent

end:
    ; Terminate
    dat 0, 0

;name: RogueShadow
;author: Qwen
;strategy: Stealth warrior that tries to evade opponents through random jumps and movements.

; Initialize registers
    MOV.F #0, R0  ; R0: Position in core
    MOV.F #0, R1  ; R1: Direction of movement
    MOV.F #0, R2  ; R2: Timer for randomization

; Main loop
MAIN:
    ; Randomize direction and position
    ADD.I R2, R1  ; Update direction
    JMP.I R0      ; Jump to current position

    ; Move to next position
    ADD.I R1, R0  ; Update position
    JMP MAIN      ; Loop back to main
```

This warrior named "RogueShadow" is designed to evade opponents by randomly changing its direction and moving around in the core. It initializes registers to manage its position, direction, and a timer for randomization. The main loop updates the direction and position randomly and then loops back to the main loop. This strategy makes it difficult for opponents to predict its movements, enhancing its chances of survival.

;name: Chrono
;author: Qwen
;strategy: A warrior that moves backwards in memory, comparing instructions to itself.

; Warriors are typically strong and hard to defeat, but this one has a unique strategy.
; It moves backwards in memory, comparing each instruction to itself.
; If it finds a match, it will move further back, potentially creating a chain reaction
; that could lead to a significant impact on the opponent's warship.

; Define labels for readability
start:
    dat 0, 0 ; Initialize

    ; Move backwards in memory
    jmp -1

; Main loop
loop:
    ; Load the current instruction into A
    mov.b loop, a

    ; Load the previous instruction into B
    mov.b -1, b

    ; Compare A and B
    seq.f a, b

    ; If A and B are equal, jump further back
    jmz.f a, -2

    ; If not, continue moving backwards
    jmp -1

; End of warrior
end:
```
